Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
tips: Keep the dumbbell close and shorten the leg extension if your lower back takes over.
Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

items.description: Hold a backpack high against your chest while performing a controlled squat.
items.name: Backpack Front Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Load the backpack lightly, close all zippers, and hold or wear it securely before the first rep.
Hold a backpack high against your chest while performing a controlled squat.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a light load first and make sure lids, straps, and zippers are secure.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Cradle a backpack in the crooks of your elbows and squat with an upright torso.
items.name: Backpack Zercher Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Load the backpack lightly, close all zippers, and hold or wear it securely before the first rep.
Cradle a backpack in the crooks of your elbows and squat with an upright torso.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a light load first and make sure lids, straps, and zippers are secure.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Use a wall for light balance support while holding the bottom of a squat.
items.name: Wall-Supported Squat Hold
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and feet a comfortable step forward.
Slide down until your knees and hips are bent to a manageable angle.
Use a wall for light balance support while holding the bottom of a squat.
Hold or move as prescribed, then press through your feet and slide back up the wall.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Stand close enough to control the movement without jamming your wrists, shoulders, or back.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Hold a backpack at the chest and lower slowly until you tap a chair.
items.name: Slow Goblet Squat to Chair
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart.
Hold a backpack at the chest and lower slowly until you tap a chair.
Reach your hips back and lower until you lightly touch or hover above the chair.
Press through the floor to stand tall without rocking forward for momentum.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Use only a stable surface that will not slide, tip, or open unexpectedly.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Place one foot slightly behind the other so the front leg does more work during the squat.
items.name: Staggered-Stance Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Start with enough open floor space to move comfortably.
Place one foot slightly behind the other so the front leg does more work during the squat.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Use a split stance with the front heel slightly elevated to bias the front thigh.
items.name: Split-Stance Heel-Elevated Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Prepare the Book or low wedge so it is stable, comfortable, and easy to control.
Use a split stance with the front heel slightly elevated to bias the front thigh.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Sit back toward a chair from a slightly wider stance while shifting one hip back.
items.name: Lateral Box Squat to Chair
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart.
Sit back toward a chair from a slightly wider stance while shifting one hip back.
Reach your hips back and lower until you lightly touch or hover above the chair.
Press through the floor to stand tall without rocking forward for momentum.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Use only a stable surface that will not slide, tip, or open unexpectedly.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Hold a chair lightly while shifting into a side squat with the opposite leg long.
items.name: Chair-Assisted Cossack Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Use a sturdy chair that will not slide, tip, or fold while you move.
Hold a chair lightly while shifting into a side squat with the opposite leg long.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Use only a stable surface that will not slide, tip, or open unexpectedly.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Step up, step down, then move directly into a reverse lunge on the same side.
items.name: Step-Up to Reverse Lunge
steps: Stand facing a low, stable step or stair.
Place one whole foot on the step and brace your trunk.

Place the palm on a wall with fingers pointing down and gently straighten the elbow.
Apply light pressure until you feel a mild stretch through the wrist, hand, or forearm.
Hold while breathing calmly, then release slowly.
Repeat with the opposite hand or direction when needed.
tips: Use light pressure because wrists and fingers can be sensitive.
Keep the stretch gentle and slow.
Do not bounce or force the end range.
Breathe steadily and aim for a mild pull rather than pain.
Stand close enough to control the movement without jamming your wrists, shoulders, or back.
Warm up first or do these after activity if holding a longer static stretch.

items.name: Cossack Squat
steps: Stand in a wide stance with toes slightly turned out.
Shift your hips toward one side and bend that knee while keeping the other leg straighter.
Lower only as far as you can keep the working heel down and chest lifted.
Push through the bent-leg foot to return to center, then repeat on the other side if alternating.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Land with soft knees and stop plyometric reps before landings get loud or stiff.

items.name: Sprinter Lunge
steps: Stand tall with feet under hips and brace your trunk.
Step into the lunge with one foot and lower until both knees bend comfortably.
Keep the front knee tracking over the middle toes and your torso controlled.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Combine forward, lateral, and reverse lunges in a continuous sequence.

images.alt: Adult stands tall at the center of a faint clock-point floor guide before starting the lunge matrix sequence.

Adult performs a lateral lunge with one knee bent, the opposite leg long, and callouts for hips back, knee tracks toes, and whole foot.
Adult performs a reverse lunge with one foot stepped behind, front heel grounded, and callouts for step back, return center, and front heel down.

items.name: Lunge Matrix
steps: Stand tall and imagine points around you like numbers on a clock.
Step into the first lunge direction and lower with control.
Push back to the center before moving to the next direction.
Continue through the listed directions while keeping each rep deliberate and balanced.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Cross-Behind Lunge

Step one foot diagonally behind the other as if making a curtsy.
Bend both knees and lower straight down with control.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then repeat or switch sides.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.

items.name: Stair Climber Step-Up

tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.

items.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat Hold
steps: Stand a short step in front of a couch or chair and place the top of one foot behind you on it.
Keep most of your weight in the front foot and your torso tall or slightly inclined.
Bend the front knee and lower straight down to a comfortable depth.
Press through the front foot to rise, then switch sides after your reps.
Hold the strongest position for the target time while keeping your breathing steady.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat

items.name: Hip Hinge Drill

Brace your trunk and push your hips back as your torso tips forward.
Keep your spine long and feel a stretch or load through the hamstrings.
Drive hips forward and squeeze glutes to stand tall again.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand tall and shift most of your weight onto one leg.
Soften the working knee and hinge your hips back while your torso tips forward.
Reach your free leg or back foot behind you for balance, depending on the variation.
Squeeze the glute and hamstring of the working leg to return to standing.
Switch sides after your planned reps.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.

items.name: Hamstring Walkout
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hips lifted into a bridge.
Take small steps with your heels away from your body while keeping hips lifted.
Walk the heels back under your knees.
Lower your hips with control and repeat.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Slowly slide your heels away until your legs are nearly straight.
Pull your heels back toward your glutes by using your hamstrings.
Keep hips lifted as much as you can, then lower and reset as needed.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Press through the balls of your feet and lift your heels.
Pause at the top without rolling ankles outward.
Lower heels slowly back to the floor.

Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms resting by your sides.
Brace gently, press through your feet, and squeeze your glutes.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Feel the work in glutes or hips rather than your lower back.
Keep ribs down and pelvis controlled.
Use smaller range if your hips start to roll or twist.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Glute Bridge Hold

items.name: Tempo Push-Up
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under or slightly wider than shoulders.
Brace your trunk and keep your body in a straight line for your chosen version.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the wall, surface, or floor.
Press through your palms to return to the start position.
Use a slow count on the lowering phase, pause briefly, then return with control.
tips: Keep shoulders away from your ears and elbows controlled.
Brace your trunk so your ribs and hips move together.
Use an incline or knees-down version when full range changes your form.
Stop the set when your hips sag, rotate, or your lower back takes over.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Clap Push-Up
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under or slightly wider than shoulders.
Brace your trunk and keep your body in a straight line for your chosen version.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the wall, surface, or floor.
Press powerfully so your hands briefly leave the floor if you can land safely.
Clap quickly before placing your hands back down and landing with soft elbows.
tips: Keep shoulders away from your ears and elbows controlled.
Brace your trunk so your ribs and hips move together.
Use an incline or knees-down version when full range changes your form.
Land with soft knees and stop plyometric reps before landings get loud or stiff.
Stop the set when your hips sag, rotate, or your lower back takes over.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Open or step the legs into the listed wide stance, lunge, frog, or wall position.
Shift hips until the inner thigh feels a mild stretch.
Keep the knee and foot aligned on the bent-leg side.
Breathe, then return slowly and switch sides if needed.
tips: Keep knee and toes pointing in the same general direction.
Use a soft bend in the knee when a straight-leg stretch feels too intense.
Ease in gradually; do not bounce into hamstring, calf, or groin stretches.
Make sure the support surface is stable and positioned so you can exit easily.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.
